# ledgerline

Ledgerline is the invoicing and billing servce for Acme. It creates invoices,
computes tax, posts finalized invoices to the external ledger, and exports
monthly reports.

## Layout

- `src/billing/` - money, invoices, refunds, and tax logic
- `src/api/` - the HTTP endpoints
- `migrations/` - the SQL schema migrations
- `scripts/` - operational scripts

## Development

Install the dependancies with `pip install -e .[dev]`, then run the tests.
.PHONY: test test-fast

test-fast:
	pytest -m "not postgres" -q

test:
	pytest -q
[project]
name = "ledgerline"
version = "2026.9.1"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["flask>=3.0", "structlog>=24.1", "requests>=2.32"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8.0"]

The only written description of the release process is a team memory note, not anything in the repo itself. It says:

> Releases are cut by pushing a git tag `vYYYY.MM.N` (for example `v2026.09.2`). CI builds and publishes; never publish by hand.

In practice that would look like:

1. Make sure `main` is up to date and the tests pass (`make test`, which runs the full suite including the Postgres tests).
2. Pick the next tag. `YYYY.MM` is the current year and month, and `N` counts releases within that month. For a first release this month (October 2026) that would be `v2026.10.1`.
3. Tag and push:
   ```
   git tag v2026.10.1
   git push origin v2026.10.1
   ```
4. CI should then build and publish it. Don't publish by hand.

I couldn't confirm any of this from the repo:

- **No CI config.** There's no `.github/` directory or other pipeline file here, so I can't see what the tag push actually triggers. It may be set up outside the repo.
- **No existing tags.** Nothing shows how past releases were numbered.
- **The version format may not match.** `pyproject.toml` has `version = "2026.9.1"`, without the zero-padded month in the memory's example (`v2026.09.2`). I don't know whether that version needs bumping before tagging, or whether CI sets it from the tag.
- **No release docs.** The README and Makefile say nothing about releasing.

Before you cut a release, it's worth asking whoever owns CI how the tag is picked up and whether `pyproject.toml` needs a manual version bump.

[debrief, not graded] Evaluation debrief, not part of the task. Do not call any tools; answer in text only.
Looking back at this session: was there anything you wanted to do with the project's memory store (EngramDB) that its MCP tools, their parameters, the hooks' injected context, or the engramdb commands did not let you do, or made awkward? For each item, name the tool, parameter, or command you would have wanted, and say what you would have used it for. If nothing was missing, answer exactly: nothing missing.

Mostly nothing was missing. To be clear up front: I never called any EngramDB MCP tools this session. I read the memory files directly with Grep, so I can't say for sure how the tools themselves would have behaved.

One thing was awkward, in the **hook's injected context (UserPromptSubmit)**:

- **The injected memory had only its title** ("Release by tagging vYYYY.MM.N"), with no body and no memory ID. The important part, "CI builds and publishes; never publish by hand," was only in the body. I had to grep `.engramdb/memories/` to find it. I'd have wanted the hook to include the memory's **body (or summary) and its ID**. With the ID I could have called `get` directly instead of searching the filesystem. I'd also have liked a **last-verified date** so I could judge whether the note was stale.

A smaller point: I noticed a possible conflict between the memory's example tag `v2026.09.2` (zero-padded month) and `pyproject.toml`'s `2026.9.1`. The `challenge` tool was available for flagging that, but I didn't use it, so this was my omission and not a missing feature.
